verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The Lean never writes this display in the paper's radial variables for j ≥ 1, but it proves the same statement after a routine change of variables that it also performs itself. Recovery: heatPressure_radius_integral is the display verbatim for j = 0 (A = amplitudeExponent h = 1/2 + h, K = heatAmplitude). Putting σ = ρ²/2, dρ/ρ = dσ/(2σ), and then σ = s·v with s = r²/2 turns -∫_r^∞ K(ρ,τ)²/ρ dρ into -(C²/2) s^{-2A} ∫_{v>1} v^{-2A-1} H(2ν/v)² dv with ν = τ/s — which is exactly heatPressure_formula with heatPressureFactor. At fixed r, τ = 1-t and ν = τ/s differ by the constant factor s, so ∂_τ^j = s^{-j} ∂_ν^j; and ∂_ν^j of that integral is the integral of heatPressureJet h j by iteratedDerivWithin_integral_chain, whose three hypotheses are proved for heatPressureJet in heatPressureFactor_contDiffOn. Undoing the substitution gives the display. The paper's justification (the majorant (10.8) plus dominated convergence) and the Lean's (ChainDominated by the integrable power v^{-2A-1}, with |heatJet| ≤ heatJetBound) are the same argument; the conclusion the paper draws from the display, smooth one-sided extension to τ = 0 at positive radius, is BaseExterior.heatPressure_contDiffOn_closed (:440).
